idiom_name: struct range (inclusive endpoints) + hand-written range_contains / range_overlaps_range
implementation_notes: C has no interval type, so the classic structure is hand-written as one struct with two endpoints plus functions, and the bound convention is fixed by the constructor helpers: QEMU's include/qemu/range.h keeps inclusive lob/upb fields, encodes the empty range as lob == upb + 1 and provides range_contains, range_overlaps_range and range_contains_range beside a half-open entry point (range_set_bounds1, documented as [lob, upb_plus1)). Open-ended intervals are not representable in that shape, so a model that needs them must add a per-side flag or a sentinel endpoint - with the sentinel hazards that implies. Keep the endpoints in one struct passed by pointer or value, so the two closures of the comparison cannot be mixed up at the call site.
pitfalls: The empty range is a convention, not a value: with inclusive bounds QEMU encodes it as lob == upb + 1, so every operation must apply that same convention or an empty range compares as a normal one.
Half-open helpers are one subtraction away from underflow: range_set_bounds1 takes upb_plus1, and computing it as 0 for an unsigned endpoint wraps to UINT64_MAX and turns the range into 'everything'.
Passing lob and upb as two separate parameters reintroduces exactly the mixed-convention bug the struct removes; always pass the struct.
Containment over float endpoints needs an explicit convention for NaN, because every comparison with NaN is false and the range then contains nothing at all.
